A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-F support reliable comparison, including matching content across figure renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original fine-tuning and benchmark evaluations of 56 base models, additional results for 36 instruction/chat models, and robustness and causal analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative analyses of changes in model rankings on GSM8K and MMLU.

M1.justification: Both versions propose the same adjustment: fine-tune each compared model on the same sufficient task-relevant data before evaluation. The fine-tuning procedure and model components are unchanged.

E1.justification: Training sources and evaluated tasks are retained, including MMLU, GSM8K, ARC, HellaSwag, and the five additional benchmarks in Appendix D. The new ranking analyses reuse existing MMLU and GSM8K evaluations.

E2.justification: The model lists, control/treatment comparisons, and Pythia–Llama 2–Qwen 1.5 family comparison are unchanged. Newly cited research is discussed without adding evaluated comparison methods.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 adds mean and maximum rank displacement as evaluation measures for the existing before/after fine-tuning comparisons. Existing benchmark metrics, shot counts, model cohorts, training budgets, and appendix evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 adds a focused analysis of how adjustment changes individual-model rankings, in Section 4.2 and Appendix E. Existing hyperparameter, temporal-cutoff, language-mixture, task-format, and emergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 reports significance and standard errors without specifying model-family clustering. v3 Section 2.2 explicitly states that significance calculations use clustered standard errors with each model family as a group. This newly documents the estimation procedure; it does not establish that the estimator or number of runs changed.

E6.justification: v3 newly reports average/maximum rank shifts of 7.7/21 places for GSM8K and 4.8/16 for MMLU, supported by Figures 7 and 18. Previously reported benchmark results, regression summaries, and appendix findings are retained.

T1.justification: The regression formulation in Equation 1 and the causal assumptions, structural equations, and derivations in Appendix B remain unchanged. Edits to their explanatory wording do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: Section 1.1 adds an explicit contribution concerning changes in individual-model rankings on MMLU and GSM8K, extending the earlier emphasis on model-family comparisons. The central claims about confounded evaluation, emergence, and the fine-tuning remedy remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 interprets test-task training as a potentially primary mechanism behind improved compute efficiency and adds the accessibility benefits of smaller, extensively pretrained models. It also supplies a concrete data-filtering example for the existing data-quality interpretation. The stated limitations and causal qualifications are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix A retains the same model repositories, optimizer and learning-rate settings, precision, batch/context sizes, hardware, and GPU-hour estimates. Code and fine-tuned-model access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to Hardt (2024), Ruan et al. (2024), Rogers and Luccioni (2024), and Gadre et al. (2024), connecting the work to rankings, observational scaling, and emergence debates. These are targeted positioning additions.

P1.justification: The revision makes localized grammar and wording corrections, inserts Section 4.2 on model rankings, renumbers the progress subsection, and broadens Appendix E's heading. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 adds ranking diagrams in Figures 7 and 18 and changes the treatment-group color in Figure 3. Existing figures and tables are retained, with limited resizing, relocation, reflow, and renumbering.

improvement.justification: The ranking analyses make the consequences for model selection explicit, while the clustered-standard-error disclosure improves statistical transparency. Targeted editing and related-work additions also improve clarity and context. These are useful, limited gains: the underlying method, experimental coverage, principal results, and causal assumptions remain unchanged.
